Limb reductions and orofacial clefts define syndrome; developmental disability and cataracts each 30-79%. Cap excludes sparse hair and cardiovascular malformations.
Infection-associated granulomatous plaques chiefly affect urinary tract, also intestine; skin inflammation/ulcers annotated 80-99%, although frequencies appear site dependent.
Entrapment directly compresses and impairs peripheral nerves; adjacent musculoskeletal structures are not necessarily diseased.
Neurodevelopmental disability, congenital contractures and muscle atrophy define syndrome. Oculomotor apraxia is neurologic; structural eye findings are occasional.
Clonal mast-cell proliferation confined to skin defines cutaneous mastocytosis; mediator symptoms do not establish damage to other organs.
Phalangeal and hip epiphyseal dysplasia define disease; hypodontia and delayed tooth eruption occur in 30-79%.
Carcinoma originates in appendix. Neuroendocrine differentiation does not establish endocrine gland disease; common spread remains gastrointestinal or outside the axes.
Mitochondrial depletion with liver failure in 2/2; congestive heart failure in 1/2. Hepatocerebral name alone and lethargy do not establish CNS damage.
Abnormal tissue mass arises from the intestinal wall and protrudes into its lumen.
CASP14-related congenital ichthyosis affects epidermal keratinization and causes scaling; no established extracutaneous involvement.
Mitochondrial encephalomyopathy and lactic acidosis define MELAS; sensorineural hearing loss occurs in 30-79%. Visual loss may be cortical; cardiac damage less common.
Impaired cerebral recognition and spatial navigation cause visual agnosia; this does not establish disease of the eye.
Fragile X syndrome ancestry supports a neurodevelopmental disorder; no subtype-specific evidence establishes additional organ damage.
Brittle sparse hair and intellectual disability characterize Sabinas syndrome; phenotype frequencies are unspecified. Occasional nail dystrophy shares the skin axis.
Complement regulatory deficiency causes cutaneous angioedema; bowel and airway swelling is episodic. A single neuropathy report does not establish common nerve damage.
Umbrella concept defined by disease of bones, joints, skeletal muscle or associated locomotor connective tissues.
Defined by neurodevelopmental impairment, epilepsy, ataxia and other cerebral or cerebellar dysfunction; no established common extracerebral damage.
Exocrine pancreatic failure, cytopenias and metaphyseal dysplasia define disease; developmental delay in 6/6. Cap excludes high myopia reported in 2/6.
Developmental and skeletal abnormalities define syndrome; hypodontia 2/4, cleft palate 1/3 and hearing loss 1/3. Cap excludes strabismus in 15/48.
Puumala hantavirus infection causes characteristic renal injury and thrombocytopenic hemorrhagic illness; no other common direct organ damage established.
BRCA1-associated susceptibility chiefly concerns breast and ovarian cancers, whose organs have no axis; predisposition does not establish current organ damage.
Follicular keratosis and inflammation cause facial skin atrophy, scarring and eyebrow hair loss; eyebrow location does not establish eye involvement.
Inherited platelet GPVI dysfunction impairs collagen-induced aggregation; bruising and mucosal bleeding do not establish damage to additional organs.
High ambient pressure produces central nervous system dysfunction with tremor, impaired cognition and seizures; nausea and dizziness add no organ axis.
